narrator.name: BitMind (SN34)
narrator.role: Subnet team; Ken Jon Miyachi, co-founder and CEO, speaks for it; Dylan Uys, co-founder and head of AI
narrator.one_line: Deepfake and AI-content detection subnet launched in 2024, rebuilt in late 2024 as GAS, a generative adversarial engine where generator miners forge and detector miners catch; its enterprise site sells a trust layer and rarely says Bittensor, while its founder tells the press Bittensor is the decentralised network where hundreds of developers compete to build the best detector.

statements.quote: Deepfake detection is one of the toughest challenges in computer vision because different generative models create various types of fake images or videos
statements.context: The team's August 2024 recap on the BitMindAI Medium publication, explaining the problem after the subnet's first weeks on mainnet; reached through a text proxy because Medium blocks direct fetches.

statements.quote: BitMind's decentralized architecture is well-suited to this problem. By leveraging a network of diverse models and miners, we can continuously adapt and improve deepfake detection methods
statements.context: Same August 2024 recap, giving the reason a subnet fits the problem.

statements.quote: The incentive mechanism we implemented has effectively rewarded accurate deepfake detection models while mitigating malicious gaming
statements.context: Same August 2024 recap, reporting on the first month of mining, alongside a note about organic innovation from miners outperforming the base model.

statements.quote: BitMind's mission is to create the best deepfake detection solution on the market, demonstrating the potential of decentralized AI and building the infrastructure for AI engineers to develop powerful end-user applications.
statements.context: Opening mission statement of the September 2024 recap on the team's Medium publication.

statements.quote: We built the deepfake detection subnet on Bittensor (Subnet 34) which incentivizes identifying and mitigating AI-generated image content.
statements.context: Same September 2024 recap, describing the subnet in one line before listing applications built on its output.

statements.quote: Subnet 34 has transformed from a distributed inference network into GAS, a self-sustaining Generative Adversarial Engine that co-evolves detectors, generators, benchmarks, and data in a single, incentive-aligned loop.
statements.context: Ken Jon Miyachi's post on the BitMind blog announcing the GAS redesign of the subnet.

source.title: GAS: Subnet 34 Becomes a Generative Adversarial Engine

statements.quote: The long-term goal is simple: turn SN34 into the default engine for trustworthy AIGC detection, an open network that continuously produces verifiable models and delivers them securely through private, production-ready infrastructure.
statements.context: Closing goal in Ken Jon Miyachi's GAS post; the same post lists mining cost, denial-of-service attacks and data privacy as reasons for moving from live miner endpoints to model submission.

source.title: GAS: Subnet 34 Becomes a Generative Adversarial Engine

statements.quote: In 2023, we had around 500,000 deepfakes circulating online. Now, we're looking at 8 million in 2025.
statements.context: Ken Jon Miyachi, BitMind CEO, in an interview with Omar Faridi of Crowdfund Insider, sizing the deepfake problem.

source.title: BitMind CEO Shares Insights On Deepfake Detection And How Decentralized Networks May Enhance The Process

statements.quote: The fundamental problem is that conventional detectors are static while generative AI is dynamic.
statements.context: Ken Jon Miyachi in the Crowdfund Insider interview, on why traditional detection fails.

source.title: BitMind CEO Shares Insights On Deepfake Detection And How Decentralized Networks May Enhance The Process

statements.quote: Instead of one team trying to keep up with thousands of deepfake creators, we've built BitMind on top of Bittensor, the decentralized network where hundreds of developers can come and compete to create the best detection algorithms, with automatic rewards for superior performance.
statements.context: Ken Jon Miyachi in the Crowdfund Insider interview, asked how a decentralised network helps detection; his fullest public description of Bittensor.

source.title: BitMind CEO Shares Insights On Deepfake Detection And How Decentralized Networks May Enhance The Process

statements.quote: Traditional systems hit around 69% accuracy on real-world deepfakes, while our latest benchmarks reached 88%. And unlike static systems, we're continuously improving.
statements.context: Ken Jon Miyachi in the Crowdfund Insider interview, giving the accuracy comparison BitMind repeats across its press.

source.title: BitMind CEO Shares Insights On Deepfake Detection And How Decentralized Networks May Enhance The Process

statements.quote: building trustworthy AI detection technology that protects users and organizations from synthetic media threats
statements.context: Ken Jon Miyachi's roadmap post on the BitMind blog, stating the company's purpose; the post does not mention Bittensor or Subnet 34.

source.title: BitMind Roadmap: Building the Future of Trustworthy AI Detection

statements.quote: The most authoritative AI fraud detection by building a dynamic, self-evolving service that instantly adapts to new threats.
statements.context: Mission line on the BitMind Overview page of docs.bitmind.ai, undated, copyright 2026, read 15 September 2026.

statements.quote: Decentralized AI (DeAI) network that realizes a continuous, dynamic, incentivized competition for producing accurate detection models … Generators push realism; discriminators improve detection — both co-evolve under aligned incentives.
statements.context: Architecture Summary page of docs.bitmind.ai describing Subnet 34; two lines joined with an ellipsis; undated, copyright 2026.

statements.quote: BitMind secures the data your business depends on. We verify the authenticity of every data point before your AI acts on it … The trust layer for enterprises
statements.context: Headline copy on bitmind.ai, copyright 2026 BitMind Holdings Limited, read 15 September 2026; the homepage does not mention Bittensor or Subnet 34.

metaphors.label: engine
metaphors.lineage_notes: GAS as a name; the engine frame recurs in the 2026 docs as a self-evolving service.

metaphors.label: co-evolution
metaphors.wording: co-evolves detectors, generators, benchmarks, and data in a single, incentive-aligned loop
metaphors.lineage_notes: Borrowed from GAN training; the Bittensor twist is that the two sides are paid miners.

metaphors.label: competition
metaphors.wording: hundreds of developers can come and compete to create the best detection algorithms
metaphors.lineage_notes: Foundation-era framing of subnets as competitions; also in Affine (sn120-004) and Ridges (sn62-003).

metaphors.label: layer
metaphors.lineage_notes: Enterprise-software framing; Hippius uses layer for memory (see sn75 coverage).

metaphors.label: self-evolving
metaphors.wording: a dynamic, self-evolving service that instantly adapts to new threats

foundation.mission.summary: Build the best deepfake detection on the market and, in doing so, demonstrate decentralised AI; later phrased as trustworthy detection protecting users and organisations from synthetic media.

foundation.vision.summary: Make SN34 the default engine for trustworthy AI-generated-content detection: an open network producing verifiable models delivered through private infrastructure.

problem.cultural.summary: Deepfakes went from half a million in 2023 to eight million in 2025.

problem.market.summary: Detectors are static while generative AI is dynamic, and detectors trained on one generator fail on others.

opportunity.summary: The explosion in deepfake volume is the tailwind the founder cites.

audience.summary: Enterprises and organisations first; the 2026 site speaks to businesses whose AI acts on data, and the subnet's own miners appear only in docs and GitHub.

positioning.category.summary: For the subnet: a deepfake detection subnet, then a generative adversarial engine, then a trust layer for enterprises. For the network: the decentralised network where hundreds of developers compete for automatic rewards.

positioning.differentiator.summary: A network of diverse models and miners that adapts continuously, against static single-team detectors.

positioning.reason.summary: Bittensor lets hundreds of developers compete with automatic rewards, so detection improves as fast as generation.

positioning.against.summary: Conventional, static detectors and single teams trying to keep up with thousands of deepfake creators.

value.functional.summary: Higher accuracy on real-world deepfakes (88 percent against 69) and verification of every data point before an AI acts on it.

messaging.h1.summary: The best deepfake detection on the market, demonstrating the potential of decentralised AI; by 2026, the most authoritative AI fraud detection through a self-evolving service.

messaging.proof.summary: Miners beating the base model in the first month, an incentive mechanism that resisted gaming, and benchmark accuracy figures.

language.term.summary: GAS (Generative Adversarial Engine), detectors and generators as miner types, AIGC detection, DeAI.

subnet.self.summary: A deepfake detection subnet that became GAS: generator miners forge synthetic media, detector miners submit models, validators evaluate both, and the whole loop co-evolves under aligned incentives.

subnet.network.summary: Bittensor is the decentralised network where developers compete for automatic rewards; the subnet exists partly to demonstrate the potential of decentralised AI. On the enterprise site the network is not named.

words_avoided: Bittensor and Subnet 34 on the 2026 homepage and the 2025 roadmap post

coinages.meaning: Generative Adversarial Subnet or Engine: the late 2024 redesign in which generator and detector miners compete in one loop.
The 2026 category claim for the company product built on the subnet's models.

genealogy.summary: At launch the team wrote for the Bittensor community in Medium recaps: the mission was the best deepfake detector on the market while demonstrating the potential of decentralised AI, and the subnet's fit was a network of diverse models and miners that adapts continuously [sn34-004] [sn34-002] [sn34-003]. In November 2024 Miyachi renamed the mechanism GAS, a generative adversarial engine, and set the long-term goal of SN34 as the default engine for trustworthy AIGC detection [sn34-006] [sn34-007].

In press interviews Miyachi framed Bittensor as the decentralised network where hundreds of developers compete for automatic rewards, set against static detectors and single teams, and led with accuracy numbers [sn34-010] [sn34-009] [sn34-011]. The October 2025 roadmap post describes trustworthy detection technology without naming Bittensor [sn34-012].
genealogy.shift: The network moves from mission statement to supporting argument; the company voice starts to separate from the subnet voice.

genealogy.summary: The 2026 homepage sells a trust layer for enterprises and does not say Bittensor; the docs keep the subnet language, calling SN34 a DeAI network running a continuous incentivized competition where generators and discriminators co-evolve [sn34-015] [sn34-013] [sn34-014].
genealogy.shift: Two registers: enterprise trust layer on the front page, adversarial competition in the docs.

relations.note: Describes Bittensor in the foundation's competition-and-rewards language rather than in the founder's market or commodity language.
Both frame the subnet as a continuous incentivized competition with anti-gaming as a proof point.
